items.title: RED repro locks the poisoning scenario before any fix
items.context: Un-gameable failing test: submit a quorum at material M1; land a commit that changes materialHash but NOT storyFilesHash; run quorum_submit again. Today the second submit is accepted and the escalation floor then reports every planned round invalid with 'duplicate host/session/key identity'. The RED assertion is that the second submit must be REFUSED while the standing quorum still evaluates ok.
items.userSees: A smoke/unit test that fails on current main by demonstrating the accepted redundant resubmit and the resulting all-rounds-invalid floor collapse.

happy.desc: Submit rounds=3 quorum at M1, commitMainDrift (materialHash changes, storyFilesHash unchanged), call quorum_submit again -> on unfixed code the second submit is accepted and evaluateHostVerdictRounds reports all rounds invalid (duplicate host/session/key identity); RED test asserts the second submit must be REFUSED -> fails on current main, passes after fix; WHY: proves the poisoning scenario is real and the repro is un-gameable

Assert currentStoryFilesHash(root) before commitMainDrift === currentStoryFilesHash(root) after commitMainDrift inside the RED check -> equality holds; WHY: the repro invariant (storyFilesHash stability across main-merge) must be asserted in-test so the fixture cannot silently degrade into a shape that does not match the real B-bf52 incident

edge.desc: commitMainDrift helper writes only to a non-story-diff file (main-drift.ts) and merges main -> assert zero story-owned file blobs changed (storyFilesHash equality is necessary but not sufficient; the helper must also not touch any story-diff file that would mask the predicate gap); WHY: if the helper accidentally touches a story file the RED repro shape diverges from the real incident

Existing green check allows a fresh quorum after a material change (commitMaterialChange edits index.ts, storyFilesHash changes) -> still passes after RED test is added with no regression; WHY: confirms the RED test addition does not break the existing same-material-refusal and fresh-quorum-allowed checks

adversarial.desc: RED test must assert BOTH the poisoning path (second submit accepted, no throw) AND the consequence (floor collapse: validRoundCount === 0, invalidRounds contain duplicate host/session/key identity) on unfixed code -> a test that fails for any other reason (e.g. unrelated throw, wrong assertion target) is not a valid RED repro; WHY: prevents gaming by writing a test that fails incidentally while the actual poisoning path is untested

RED test must write no leftover state that poisons subsequent checks in the same smoke run -> use withFreshFixture isolation or equivalent teardown, capture hostVerdictEventCount and verdictFileCount before/after; WHY: RED repro that corrupts shared fixture state causes cascading false failures in the test suite

verificationEvidence.note: Check 'refuses a redundant re-submit when the standing quorum drift-accepts': RED-locked pre-fix at commit c9090580 (assert.fail with poisoning forensics), green post-fix with the refusal asserted.
Same check asserts currentStoryFilesHash is byte-identical before/after commitMainDrift (incident precondition) and materialHash moved.
commitMainDrift helper commits only packages/main/src/main-drift.ts on the fixture main branch, then merges - no story-diff file is touched.
Full smoke suite green (58 checks) including every pre-existing check - the RED addition broke nothing.

The check asserts BOTH the refusal (post-fix) AND, on the pre-fix path, proves the floor collapse via eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade + evaluateHostVerdictRounds forensics (validRounds=0 invalidRounds=3) - un-gameable in both directions.
withFreshFixture chdir-restore + rmSync teardown isolates the RED fixture; all later checks in the same run stay green.

items.title: Align the quorum_submit duplicate guard with the floor's drift-accept predicate
items.context: In handlers/quorum-submit.ts, the guard must treat a committed verdict on a planned runId as colliding when it would be accepted by the floor at evaluation time: same materialDigest OR (stale materialDigest but storyFilesHash equal to the current storyFilesHash). The refusal message must state that the existing quorum still drift-accepts and nothing needs resubmitting.
items.userSees: quorum_submit refuses the redundant resubmit after a materialHash-only drift with a message naming the standing valid quorum; a genuinely new quorum (storyFilesHash changed) is still allowed.

happy.desc: Submit rounds=3 quorum at M1, commitMainDrift (materialHash changes, storyFilesHash unchanged), call quorum_submit again -> second submit throws refusal with message containing drift-accept explanation and naming the standing valid quorum; WHY: core fix verification that the guard now matches the floor drift-accept predicate

Submit rounds=3 quorum at M1, commitMaterialChange (edits story-diff file index.ts, storyFilesHash changes), call quorum_submit again -> submit succeeds, emits 6 new verdicts; WHY: genuine new material must not be blocked by the widened guard

edge.desc: Committed host_verdict event has empty or missing storyFilesHash field -> guard treats as non-colliding on the drift-accept branch (falls through to materialDigest-only check, which also does not match after commitMainDrift) -> second submit is allowed; WHY: legacy events without storyFilesHash must not trigger false-positive collision via normalizeString matching empty-to-empty

Same materialDigest exact match (no drift, no commitMainDrift) -> guard still refuses with existing same-material message unchanged; WHY: regression check that the original guard branch is preserved alongside the new drift-accept branch

Refusal message on drift-accept branch contains the standing quorum information (runIds, materialDigest of standing verdicts) and points at review_escalation_status; WHY: the message must teach the caller that nothing is missing so they do not attempt workarounds

adversarial.desc: Two sequential commitMainDrift calls (double merge-main, two different non-story commits) before re-submit -> guard still refuses because storyFilesHash is unchanged through both drifts; WHY: multiple sequential drifts must not circumvent the guard by accumulating state

Attacker commits a file that exists in BOTH the story diff and main, then merges main which changes that file -> storyFilesHash changes -> guard allows resubmit; verify this is correct behavior (genuinely new story material, not a false bypass); WHY: boundary between drift-accept (storyFilesHash unchanged) and genuine story-material change (storyFilesHash changed) must be airtight

Guard refusal on drift-accept branch writes zero host_verdict events, zero verdict files, and does not advance HEAD -> assert hostVerdictEventCount, verdictFileCount, and git rev-parse HEAD are all unchanged; WHY: a guard that refuses but leaks partial state (e.g. events written before throw) would corrupt future quorum attempts

verificationEvidence.note: Refusal message matched against /quorum_submit refuses: .*drift-accept/i in the drift-accept check.
Check 'allows a fresh quorum after a material change' (story-diff file change moves storyFilesHash) still green under the new guard.
Check 'blank storyFilesHash on committed legacy verdicts is no-signal for the drift branch': field stripped from committed events, resubmission after drift proceeds (OQ-1 no-signal).
Check 'refuses a same-material re-submit and writes no new verdicts' passes unchanged - branch (a) message and behavior preserved.
Drift-branch message content asserted via regex; message names standing runIds, older material(s), current storyFilesHash, poisoning consequence, and points at review_escalation_status.
Check 'a second main drift does not circumvent the drift-accept refusal': refusal holds across two successive merges; still exactly six verdicts.
Check 'a story-owned file change after main drift makes the re-quorum genuine again': once storyFilesHash moves the fresh quorum is allowed (boundary).
Refusal leaks zero state: host_verdict event count and verdict file count asserted unchanged after the refusal.

items.title: Official recovery command for poisoned quorum rounds
items.context: New command (quorum_prune) that, for a story, identifies host_verdict duplicate events on the same runId + host/session/key identity in the committed process-events.jsonl, and removes the losing set (default: the set whose materialDigest no longer resolves; explicit selector otherwise). Must support --dryRun, write a backup of the jsonl before editing, and commit the metadata change. Formalizes the manual B-bf52 surgery (commit 255eefd289).
items.userSees: lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists the duplicate verdict events and which set would be removed; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits, and the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level.
excludes: any change to floor/escalation acceptance semantics

happy.desc: Inject duplicate host_verdict events on the same runId + host/session/key identity into committed process-events.jsonl (simulating B-bf52 poisoning), run quorum_prune with dryRun:true -> output lists the exact duplicate verdict events (verdictId, runId, host, materialDigest, timestamp) and which set would be removed vs which survives; WHY: validates the discovery and reporting logic

Run quorum_prune with apply:true on the poisoned fixture -> backup file created alongside process-events.jsonl with timestamp in name, duplicates removed from jsonl, metadata committed; then evaluateReviewEscalation returns full-3x2 assurance level (validRoundCount >= 3); WHY: end-to-end recovery path verification

quorum_prune is registered in command-catalog.ts, lattice-cli.ts, and command-policy.ts and is accessible via the CLI (lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun) -> command dispatches without unknown-command error; WHY: wiring verification across all 5 integration points

edge.desc: No duplicate host_verdict events found for any runId -> quorum_prune refuses with a clear nothing-to-prune message and writes no backup, no mutation, no commit; WHY: prevents accidental mutation when quorum state is clean

Working tree is dirty (uncommitted changes in tracked files) -> quorum_prune refuses before any file I/O with pre-dirty refusal message; WHY: dirty-tree guard prevents interleaving with uncommitted work

Triple-duplicate (3 host_verdict events for same runId + identity) -> keeps exactly 1 event per group (the one matching keep selector, default newest-material) and removes the other 2; WHY: handles more-than-double duplication gracefully
runIds filter is provided -> only duplicates on the specified runIds are pruned, other runId duplicates are left untouched; WHY: selective pruning for targeted recovery

adversarial.desc: process-events.jsonl contains interleaved non-host_verdict events (e.g. review_run, review_pass) between host_verdict duplicates -> all non-host_verdict events are preserved unmodified in the rewritten file, in their original order; WHY: pruning must only remove host_verdict duplicates, never corrupt other event types or reorder the log

Run quorum_prune with keep:oldest-material -> removes the newer-material duplicates instead of the default newest-material ones; verify the surviving events have the older materialDigest; WHY: exercises the selector inversion and proves it is not hardcoded

Process-events.jsonl exists but is untracked or only staged (not committed) -> quorum_prune refuses with a message about uncommitted events file; WHY: the command must only operate on committed state to avoid rewriting in-flight data

Backup file from a previous quorum_prune run already exists at the timestamped path -> the new backup uses a distinct timestamp or otherwise does not overwrite the previous backup; WHY: prevents loss of earlier recovery evidence if pruning is run multiple times

verificationEvidence.note: Check 'quorum_prune dry-run lists the poisoned duplicates without mutating'.
Check 'quorum_prune apply removes the losing set, backs up, and the floor returns to full-3x2'.
Check 'quorum_prune resolves as a registered CLI command (catalog + policy wired)'; scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs passes with the new fact row and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS entry.
Check 'quorum_prune refuses when there is nothing to prune'.
Check 'quorum_prune apply refuses on a dirty tree before any mutation'.
Check 'quorum_prune keeps exactly one event per group for a triple-duplicate'.
Check 'quorum_prune runIds filter prunes only the specified runIds'.
Check 'quorum_prune preserves interleaved non-host_verdict lines byte-identically'.
Check 'quorum_prune keep:oldest-material inverts which duplicate survives'.
Check 'quorum_prune refuses an uncommitted process-events file'.
Check 'quorum_prune never overwrites a previous run backup'.
